prompt:
Normalize the one contact record in the note. Return only a bare JSON object with exactly name, phone, email, company, country, each a string or null.

Use only the record’s labeled lines (label aliases allowed; separators include colon, equals, and tab). Trim values and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Absent, empty, or case-insensitive -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD means null, except for the country fallback below. Never use notes, signatures, domains, or legal suffixes to infer missing values.

Assign country from its own line. For other lines, route any value containing @ to email; route a value to phone if, after stripping leading tel: and a trailing extension, it has at least seven digits and contains only digits, spaces, or + - ( ) . /. Extensions are ext., ext, x, #, or extension followed by extension digits. If the name-labeled value ends in a legal suffix and the company-labeled value does not, swap them. Legal suffixes (case-insensitive; optional preceding comma): AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda.

Name: reorder Last, First at the first comma; drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, Prof (any case, optional dot); uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of every space- or hyphen-separated part. Company: strip the trailing legal suffix and optional comma; trim and apply the same casing per space-separated word only. Email: strip surrounding angle brackets and leading mailto: wherever nested, then lowercase the whole address without otherwise changing it. Preserve Unicode and diacritics; do not transliterate.

Country: normalize English, Swedish, or German names, alpha-2/alpha-3 codes, or common aliases (any case) to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. UK/Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA/U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ.

Phone: strip tel: and the extension. A leading + or 00, ignoring an opening parenthesis, means international. Convert leading 00 to +, drop international (0), and remove spaces, dashes, dots, slashes, and parentheses. Keep the international calling code regardless of the country line. If country is missing, an international calling code uniquely identifying one country supplies it; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave it null. For a national number, remove formatting and one leading trunk 0, then prepend + and the normalized country’s calling code; without country, return null for phone. All non-null phones are E.164: + and digits only.
